contributions.statement: If MCP servers run as replicas behind a gateway, stateful sessions make session-affinity routing the dominant per-request cost (≈75% of latency, 3x CPU), and tail latency grows ~8x at four gateway instances from session-store misses. Prefer stateless MCP servers (stateless Streamable HTTP) for anything replicated.
contributions.evidence: §6.4, Fig. 14: single instance 4.59 ms mean (session mgmt 3.45 ms), 85% vs 27% CPU; 4 instances P99 55.6 ms vs stateless ≤3.3 ms flat.

contributions.statement: If tool retrieval is ever needed over a catalog whose tool names encode domain identifiers, fuse BM25 with dense retrieval (RRF) rather than dense-only, and return ~15 candidates.
contributions.evidence: §6.3: Recall@15 98.2% hybrid vs 83.1% dense vs 67.7% BM25 at 3,616 tools; sharp gain from top-10 to top-15 (Fig. 12); ToolBench gain small (97.5 vs 95.5).

contributions.statement: At ~15 tools, inlining every schema still gives ~92% single-tool selection; degradation becomes material only at hundreds of tools, so retrieval or gateway infrastructure is unwarranted for a small catalog.
contributions.evidence: §6.2, Fig. 9(d): ToolBench naive 92.4% at N=15 → 78.2% at N=640; Qwen3.6-plus only, single run.

contributions.statement: Precompute prerequisite tool chains from schema dependencies so retrieval returns executable chains, not just the target tool.
contributions.evidence: §7 Lesson 3, Table 5: 100% completeness vs 56-73% iterative discovery, but completeness is near-tautological for a cache built from the same dependency graph.

reason: Beyond the system tour, two measured points matter to a small-catalog team. Expose-all is still fine at 15 tools, and stateful MCP replication carries a large routing tax. The hybrid-retrieval heuristic matters only at scale. Vendor self-evaluation on proprietary data caps everything at moderate.
